scope.historical_pull_request_state: MERGED; not rewritten by this change
scope.summary: Repair the confirmed Stack #200 findings against current source. No capture, promotion, merge, or readiness transition is claimed.

changes.finding: Derive TLS identity from the measured binary
repair: Each compiled layer consumer answers a `tls-identity` request from `TlsRuntime.info()`; capture records that record per layer as `artifact.<layer>.tls_provider` and as the report-level `tls_provider`.
The former hard-coded environment `TLS` string is removed; comparison uses `environment.tls_provider` plus the recorded provider command output.

`validate_environment()` reconstructs `cjc`, `cjpm`, `cpu`, `uname`, `kernel`, `compiler_digest`, `runtime_binaries` and `runtime_environment` from retained metadata commands, including the `environment-witness` subcommand, and rejects an edited block.
Every sample records the digest of the executed binary; its `argv[0]` must equal the recorded layer `command_path`, so an unrecorded executable cannot be attributed to the recorded build.
`cjpm` participates in the compared environment identity.
Comparison additionally requires identical `probe_sources`, `task_source_digests`, `workload_counts`, `scenario_contracts` and `tls_provider`; any mismatch is `INCONCLUSIVE`.

changes.finding: Validate work counts for every benchmark scenario
repair: `SCENARIO_CONTRACTS` declares operations, expected rejections and regime for all 33 scenarios, recorded as `scenario_contracts` and rechecked on load.
`validate_workload_sample()` no longer returns early for HTTP/SSE/WebSocket cases; it validates command arguments and sample accounting for every scenario.
`http_observed` requires `enabled` plus `metrics.observation_enabled == true`; `http_unobserved` requires `disabled` plus the false metric.
`warmup_process_rounds` is enforced for every scenario in every declared warmup round.
`regime` is part of `summarize().contract`, so regime mismatch yields `INCONCLUSIVE`.

changes.finding: Reject repeated raw executions within one report
repair: Execution identity is the canonical digest of the validated native JSON record (`canonical_execution_identity`).
A capture log must contain exactly one line; appended diagnostics are rejected instead of changing the identity.
Duplicate raw executions inside one report are rejected; cross-report overlap uses the same canonical identities and must be disjoint.
`evaluate_read_buffer()` pairs the two cohorts by recorded `round`, so serialized order cannot change the sign test.

changes.finding: Handle truncated command arrays as inconclusive
repair: Report loading validates `argv` length and scenario arguments before indexing; truncated arrays raise `ValueError` rather than `IndexError`.
CPU/environment metadata is validated while loading the report, before any comparison.

The whole compare path, including environment comparison and classification, runs inside the guarded block, which now also catches `IndexError` and `AttributeError`, and always writes the documented `INCONCLUSIVE` decision file.
